title: Quentin and the Parish
premise: Emrys Vasquez, a concierge whose gift for noticing has quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays in advance to prove a murder that hasn't happened yet — the killing of parish archivist Quentin Hale, scheduled for the night of the church's tercentenary gala. Emrys discovers Quentin faked his own death years ago to escape testifying against the parish's beloved warden, and the client is Quentin himself, buying one last chance to surface safely. When the warden's enforcer strikes early and kills the wrong man, Emrys must find the living witness before the gala ends, choosing between protecting their own carefully hidden past and exposing a truth the whole town would rather bury. In the end Emrys delivers Quentin to the police alive, at the cost of their anonymity and their job — survival, they learn, is a price paid in memory.
about_author: Bram Amberdale spent a decade working night desks in grand hotels, collecting the small betrayals of the wealthy before turning them into fiction. They live in a coastal town much like the one in this book, and still can't stop reading other people's luggage tags.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A cash-heavy stranger books a room and hires Emrys to prove Quentin Hale won't be murdered on Saturday night — offering no name and refusing questions. Emrys's instincts scream scam, but the money matches three unsolved deaths they've never told anyone about. The beat: wary curiosity hardening into compulsion as Emrys accepts, knowing acceptance means entering the story instead of observing it.

chapters.title: The Man Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, with an intercut letter from Quentin. Digging through parish records, Emrys finds Quentin Hale buried eleven years ago — yet the client's details match him exactly. A letter reveals Quentin faked his death to flee the warden he was meant to testify against. The emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into dread when Emrys realizes someone else has found the same records, because the archive room has been searched.

chapters.title: Wrong Body, Right Night
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On gala eve, the warden's enforcer kills a young verger mistaken for Quentin, and the town closes ranks around its sainted warden. Emrys finds Quentin hiding in the hotel's forgotten fourth-floor rooms, half-mad with guilt over the dead boy. The beat: fury and tenderness entwined — Emrys must decide whether the witness who caused a death deserves saving, while the enforcer closes in on the hotel.

chapters.title: What the Bells Remember
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, climaxing during the tercentenary bells. Emrys walks Quentin through the gala crowd in plain sight, using the warden's own ritual pride as cover, and forces a public confrontation recorded by a journalist ally. The warden falls; Quentin surrenders to police; Emrys's anonymous past surfaces in the process. The final beat: bittersweet resolution — justice done, identity lost, and Emrys keeping only the memory of having finally chosen to act.
